sections.explanation: Coordinates describe quantities, not a picture of the object’s path. Label both axes and units. For a straight line y = mx + c, c is the vertical intercept and m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁). A horizontal position–time segment is stationary; a negative slope means decreasing position. Average rate over an interval is a secant slope, not an instantaneous derivative. Interpolation estimates between observations; extrapolation assumes the relationship continues beyond them.
sections.worked: Positions 3, 7 and 11 m at times 0, 2 and 4 s give slope (11 − 3)/4 = 2 m/s and s = 3 + 2t. At 3 s interpolation gives 9 m. Predicting 23 m at 10 s is extrapolation and needs the constant-rate assumption.
tasks: A position record is 0 m at 0 s, 4 m at 2 s and 4 m at 5 s. Find each segment’s slope.
Explain why stretching the vertical axis changes visual steepness but not a correctly calculated slope.
feedback: The numerical coordinate differences and units remain the same.
